meta.title: Jam Cycle Map
meta.kindNote: Only cross-functional moments are drawn. Team and pod sessions (Big Room Planning, Pitch-back, Design Share-outs, launch tier confirmation) stay in the data but are hidden.

lanes.name: Product
lanes.summary: Decides where to invest. Shapes opportunities, aligns pods during planning, keeps the business informed, and feeds product truth into the downstream documents.

lanes.name: Engineering
lanes.summary: Leads the delivery pod. Turns a selected opportunity into an implementation plan, then delivers with protected focus for six weeks.

lanes.name: Design
lanes.summary: Shapes the experience inside the pod. Designs early, shares out with the Build Org and the company, then hardens and hands off.

lanes.name: Product Marketing
lanes.summary: Owns the Launch Brief and launch tiers. Least developed lane; expect this to change as enablement matures.

lanes.name: Program & Enablement
lanes.summary: Stewards the system: inspects planning, opens and progresses the downstream documents, runs enablement sessions, and closes out the prior cycle.

activities.title: Refine selected opportunities with pods
activities.detail: Each PM works with the pods that picked their opportunity to turn the problem space into an implementation plan. Sessions are pod plus PM. Ends with the Engineering Pitch-back.

activities.title: Finish prior-cycle Launch Brief and Walkthrough/FAQ to 100%
activities.detail: New. After Engineering Demo Day the docs are around 80%. Weeks 1 and 2 bring them to complete, with the shipped behavior confirmed, so they can live in the repository of what is coming out.

activities.title: Shape and rank next-cycle opportunities
activities.detail: Discovery with customers, internal stakeholders and data. Pitch Discovery sessions bring relevant people in early. PM team sessions refine and challenge ideas, then decide what goes to Portfolio Review and in what order (ranked 1 to 20). Finalize pitches before the review.

activities.title: Keep the ledger current; feed the Launch Brief and Walkthrough/FAQ
activities.detail: Product maintains the Product Delivery Ledger item for each committed piece of work and contributes product truth to the downstream documents as delivery gets more precise.

activities.title: Opportunity intake with pod leads (forecast)
activities.detail: After Portfolio Review the engineering, design and product leads for each pod take a first pass at the opportunities the pod forecast it will pick up. Product is not in the pod; it joins when one of its items is picked. This is a surface to test whether anything would stop this becoming the official plan.

activities.title: Enablement sessions; docs to about 80%
activities.detail: Present alongside Program at the two enablement sessions. Confirm what is in production versus still building.

activities.title: Cooldown and ramp-up
activities.detail: Self-led. Cooldown is whatever gets the team refreshed: tech debt, a retro, a half day off. Ramp-up is planning with the PM, breaking down the opportunity, and writing the implementation plan. The one thing that must be true at the end: an implementation plan Product is aligned with.

activities.title: Focused delivery
activities.detail: Protected build time. Make progress visible early, test assumptions while change is still possible, push meaningful changes into the ledger before they become surprises. Ends with a shipped increment and Engineering Demo Day.

activities.title: Opportunity intake (engineering lead)
activities.detail: The pod's engineering lead joins the product and design leads for a first pass at the forecast opportunities. Secondary to delivery.

activities.title: Design V1
activities.detail: First version of the designs for the selected opportunity, in parallel with pod refinement.

activities.title: Refine with the pod and PM
activities.detail: Design takes part in pod refinement sessions and the Pitch-back so the implementation plan and the design direction agree.

activities.title: Iterate, align, test
activities.detail: Iterate on V1, align with the pod and design leadership, test with users. Design Share-outs at the end of week 3, Design Demo Day at the end of week 4.

activities.title: Iterate, harden, hand off
activities.detail: Take the direction the pod landed on and make it ready: edge cases, states, handoff to engineering.

activities.title: Opportunity intake (design lead)
activities.detail: The pod's design lead joins the first pass at the forecast opportunities for next cycle.

activities.title: Support delivery; release QA in week 8
activities.detail: Answer build questions and, in the final week, QA what is about to release: what needs cleaning up before we are ready to go.

activities.title: Discuss proposed launch tiers
activities.detail: Tiers were proposed right after Portfolio Review. Weeks 1 and 2 are for conversation about what a Tier 1, 2 or 3 means for storytelling and strategy, a full eight weeks before release.

activities.title: Release notes and launch comms for shipped work
activities.detail: Placeholder. Work that landed on time rides this release; otherwise it rolls to the next. Post-cycle PMM work is not yet well defined.

activities.title: Confirm launch tier; open the Launch Brief
activities.detail: By the end of week 3 the shape of the solution is known well enough to confirm the tier. Target: 100% on the tier, launch language drafted. Percentages here are provisional.

activities.title: Product messaging framework (Tier 1 and 2)
activities.detail: Positioning, narrative, proof and what not to overstate, captured in the Launch Brief.

activities.title: Launch timing, GTM plan, packaging and pricing
activities.detail: Finalize the plan for bringing the work to market alongside the enablement sessions.

activities.title: Propose launch tiers for next cycle
activities.detail: Right after Portfolio Review, propose a tier for each confirmed opportunity so the conversation can start early.

activities.title: Inspect what we expect: every pod has PM sessions, Big Room Planning and a Pitch-back
activities.detail: Teams plan however they want, but each pod either has these in place or can say why they are unnecessary. Ends by opening the Launch Brief and Walkthrough/FAQ drafts at Delivery Kickoff.

activities.title: Close out prior-cycle enablement docs to 100%
activities.detail: Coordinate the last 20% with Product, PMM and CS/Sales owners now that the work has shipped.

activities.title: Progress the drafts; add the Design Demo Day recording
activities.detail: Each org-wide moment gets recorded and added to the Launch Brief and Walkthrough/FAQ so they build up over the cycle.

activities.title: Prepare enablement; optional early session
activities.detail: Sessions can happen any time after Design Demo Day. Some cycles have one at the start of week 6 or even week 4.

activities.title: Run enablement sessions; docs to about 80%
activities.detail: Sessions at the start of week 7 and week 8 bring the full CS and Sales teams through what is coming. Recorded and added to the docs. We call the business enabled at this point even though the final version is not yet in production.

activities.title: System health: ledger, change notices, checkpoints
activities.detail: Keep cadence, escalation paths and cross-functional clarity working. Hidden change is the failure mode, not change.

milestones.name: Jam Session Kickoff
milestones.audience: Full organization, especially the Build Org
outputs: Shared view of strategy and the selected work
milestones.detail: Opens the cycle. Happens at the same boundary as the prior cycle's Engineering Demo Day and cycle close.

milestones.name: Engineering Big Room Planning
inputs: Each pod's early thinking after first sessions with the PM
milestones.detail: A sounding board at the end of week 1. Requires that initial conversations with Product have already happened.

milestones.name: Engineering Pitch-back
milestones.audience: Pod, PM and Design (one per pod)
milestones.detail: The checkpoint that says planning is done. Every pod has one unless there is a reason it does not make sense.

milestones.name: Delivery Kickoff
milestones.audience: Full Build Org plus key stakeholders; anyone welcome
outputs: Launch Brief and Walkthrough/FAQ drafts opened
milestones.detail: Celebrates the end of planning and tells everyone what we are going for. First point where the downstream documents exist.

milestones.name: Design Share-outs
milestones.audience: Pod plus design leadership; sometimes business stakeholders
outputs: Confirmation the design is on track with the Build Org

milestones.name: Confirm Launch Tiers
inputs: Shape of the solution from planning
milestones.detail: We do not know exactly what is coming, but we know the shape of it and how big a deal to make of it.

milestones.name: Design Demo Day
outputs: Recording, added to the Launch Brief and Walkthrough/FAQ
Business can see and touch the direction
milestones.detail: Midpoint of the cycle. First time the wider business sees the product taking shape.

milestones.name: Enablement Session (optional, early)
outputs: Earlier readiness where the work allows it
milestones.detail: Some cycles run an extra session at the start of week 6 or week 4. Any time after Design Demo Day works.

milestones.name: Portfolio Review
milestones.audience: Executive team, extended leadership and key stakeholders; all PMs present and presenting
outputs: Confirmed, ranked list of work for next cycle
milestones.detail: The business says yes or no, with conversation where needed. Everything downstream for next cycle keys off this.

milestones.name: Pods Select Pitches (forecast)
outputs: Forecast of what each pod will take on
milestones.detail: A forecast, not a commitment. The whole team is not present and we are still building.

milestones.name: Enablement Session 2
milestones.detail: Start of week 8. Not 100% because the final version is not in production and the docs are partial.

milestones.name: Engineering Demo Day
outputs: Cycle closes; next cycle opens with Jam Session Kickoff
milestones.detail: Celebratory show and tell. Closes the org-wide alignment arc: Kickoff explained the strategy, Design Demo Day showed the shape, Engineering Demo Day shows what is real.

artifacts.name: Opportunity
artifacts.purpose: Product's way of pitching work: a constrained problem space leadership can evaluate and pods can shape.

artifacts.name: Pod Delivery Plan (implementation plan)
artifacts.purpose: The pod's way of confirming its plan: chosen approach, intended increment, scope, cut lines, risks.

checkpoints.label: First pass at Big Room Planning

artifacts.name: Product Delivery Ledger
artifacts.purpose: Live operational state for committed work: delivery state, changes, risks, readiness, next checkpoint.

artifacts.name: Launch Brief
artifacts.purpose: How to talk about the work: audience, positioning, what not to overstate, launch posture.

artifacts.name: Feature Walkthrough & FAQ
artifacts.owner: CS / Sales / Support owner, with Product
artifacts.purpose: How the delivered experience actually works, its limits, and how to demo, support and answer questions.

notes: The monthly CS Listening Session runs the second Friday of each month, which does not map to cycle weeks, so it is not shown.
Only whole-company, Build Org, leadership and CS & Sales moments are drawn. Team and pod sessions remain in the data, hidden.
Opportunity + Pitch Collab in the old diagram is now simply Opportunity intake (weeks 7 and 8).
Readiness percentages (80% at enablement, tier 100% by week 3) are provisional targets.
Product Marketing's lane and the post-cycle PMM work (release notes, launch comms) are placeholders pending definition.
Closing the prior cycle's docs to 100% in weeks 1 and 2 is new and not in the Notion pages yet.
Engineering Big Room Planning at the end of week 1 was missing from the Figma; it is in the data as a hidden team session.
